**Short answer:** *Maybe, but I wouldn’t call Wiggle & Snug Snug-Fit Diapers a “yes” for newborns unless you can verify the size, materials, and fit.* I couldn’t find a reliable official product page or independent newborn-specific testing/reviews for the exact “Wiggle & Snug Snug-Fit Diapers” name; searches mostly turned up unrelated products or Huggies “Snug” diapers. ([target.com](https://www.target.com/p/-/A-1013551250?utm_source=openai))

For a **newborn**, I’d only use them if they meet these checks:

- **Newborn size/weight range** — usually labeled NB or “up to ~10 lb.”
- **Soft, fragrance-free, alcohol-free/low-irritant materials** — newborn skin is sensitive; AAP recommends alcohol- and fragrance-free wipes, and frequent changes to limit irritation. ([healthychildren.org](https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/diapers-clothing/Pages/Diaper-Rash.aspx?utm_source=openai))
- **Good umbilical cord clearance** — ideally an umbilical cutout or a front that can fold down.
- **Snug but not tight fit** — no gaps at the legs, but no deep red marks on belly/thighs.
- **Absorbent enough** — leaks, blowouts, or damp-feeling skin mean they’re not a good match.
- **No rash after a trial pack** — diaper rash can be triggered by moisture, chafing, or sensitivity; change wet/dirty diapers promptly and stop using them if irritation appears. ([mayoclinic.org](https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/diaper-rash/symptoms-causes/syc-20371636?utm_source=openai))

**My practical recommendation:** buy only a **small pack first**. If your baby stays dry, has no rash, and the diaper sits below/away from the umbilical stump, they’re fine to keep using. If you see redness, leaks, chemical/fragrance smell, or poor fit, switch to a well-established newborn diaper like **Huggies Little Snugglers**, **Pampers Swaddlers**, or another fragrance-free newborn option.
